scenarios.title: A long booking, then a short one that overlaps it — refused (409) before Stripe, first booking untouched

checks.desc: the 90-min treatment is booked, paid and confirmed
its session froze duration 90, turnaround 0, 1 seat
the frozen order carries duration 90
the overlapping 30-min booking is REFUSED with 409
the guest sees "that time just filled up"
checks.detail: That time just filled up. Pick another.

checks.desc: no order was created for the refused attempt (no Stripe touched)
the first booking is untouched (still 1 seat, dur 90)

scenarios.title: Two non-overlapping 60-min treatments, back-to-back, both succeed

checks.desc: the 10:00 booking is confirmed
the 11:00 booking is confirmed
both sessions exist, each with 1 seat and duration 60

scenarios.title: A shared table still takes several bookings on the same time; the interval guard is inert for it

checks.desc: both shared bookings on the same time confirmed
the one session holds 3 seats (several bookings, same time)
an adjacent group time books fine (no false overlap)

scenarios.title: The same pair — a 60 at 09:00 then a 30 at 10:00 — both succeed with no reset, but the 30 is refused once a 30-minute reset is counted

checks.desc: with reset 0, the 60 then the back-to-back 30 both succeed
the 60-min session froze the 30-minute reset
the SAME 30 at 10:00 is now REFUSED (409) — the reset gap alone causes it
checks.detail: HTTP 409 {"ok":false,"error":"That time just filled up. Pick another."}

checks.desc: no order created for the refused attempt
the earlier booking, frozen at reset 0, is untouched by the later change

scenarios.title: A booked overlap written directly — the race the claim could let through — is refused by the exclusion constraint (23P01)

checks.desc: a 60-min booking holds the time
the overlapping booked row is REJECTED by the database
the rejection is the no-overlap exclusion constraint (23P01)
no overlapping session row exists after the refusal
